answer: In a market where AI agents trade walnut timber, saffron, and karst survey data, each seller identity must lock a bond in escrow before accepting orders. Proven nondelivery forfeits the bond to the buyer, and pending orders keep that capital locked. Creating names is cheap, but operating a thousand fraudulent sellers requires a thousand funded bonds; setting each bond above the maximum unpaid order value makes a successful scam cost more than it earns.
